title: Basic definitions and results
notice: This map records public paraphrases and Lean source locations. It does not reproduce the textbook text.

items.title: Preorders and partial orders
items.summary: Predicate-level encodings of reflexive/transitive relations and antisymmetric partial orders.

items.title: Order duals
items.summary: The dual of a partial order is again a partial order.

items.title: Order-theoretic vocabulary
items.summary: Upper/lower sets, bounds, maximal/minimal elements, largest/least elements, suprema, infima, and lattice completeness.

items.title: Elementary laws for suprema and infima
items.summary: Monotonicity and closure/union laws for suprema and infima in the local predicate formulation.

items.title: Closure systems as complete lattices
items.summary: Intersections give infima, and closure of unions gives the least closed upper bound.

items.title: Monotone maps
items.summary: Monotone maps are represented using Lean's standard `Monotone` predicate.

items.title: Fixed points in complete lattices
items.summary: A monotone self-map of a complete lattice has least and greatest fixed points.

items.title: Directed sets, ideals, filters, and chains
items.summary: Directed subsets, ideals, filters, and chain predicates used throughout the chapter.

items.title: Joins by finite nonempty joins
items.summary: The local formalization records the finite-nonempty-join decomposition target for nonempty joins.

items.title: Monotone nets and subnets
items.summary: Bundled monotone nets, subnets, and the image-supremum predicate used for directed supremum arguments.

items.title: Finite-principal lattice subnet
items.summary: Every monotone net has a cofinal subnet indexed by finite subsets, giving a lattice-shaped directed index.

items.title: Iterated directed suprema
items.summary: Diagonal and iterated directed suprema agree in the predicate formulation.

items.title: Directed-complete partial orders
items.summary: A dcpo is represented by directed completeness together with antisymmetry; the reusable directed-completeness component remains separately available.

items.title: Dcpos and chain suprema
items.summary: A poset is a dcpo iff every chain has a supremum; the hard direction is isolated behind a documented Markowsky/Iwamura axiom.

items.title: Least fixed points in pointed dcpos
items.summary: Least fixed point existence for monotone endomaps is recorded through Pataraia-style support lemmas and a documented external theorem.

items.title: Scott-continuity and strict maps
items.summary: Scott-continuity preserves directed suprema; strict maps preserve bottom in pointed dcpos.

items.title: Function spaces of continuous maps
items.summary: Scott-continuous function spaces are dcpos with pointwise order and pointwise directed suprema.

items.title: Kleene fixed point theorem
items.summary: The least fixed point of a Scott-continuous self-map is the supremum of the Kleene iteration chain, and the chosen fixpoint assignment is Scott-continuous.

items.title: Fixed-point induction
items.summary: Admissible predicates support induction over least fixed points of continuous endomaps.

items.title: Fixed point invariance
items.summary: Strict commuting squares preserve least fixed points.

items.title: Way-below relation and compactness
items.summary: The approximation relation `x ≪ y`, compact elements, and the standard lower/upper way-below sets.

items.title: Basic way-below laws
items.summary: Way-below implies order-below and is monotone in both arguments.

items.title: Bases and approximants
items.summary: Approximants relative to a candidate basis, plus raw and strengthened basis predicates.

items.title: Elementary basis facts
items.summary: Raw bases yield directed approximant sets, bases contain compact elements, and supersets of bases are bases.

items.title: Smallest basis and compact elements
items.summary: The whole carrier is a basis when any basis exists, compact elements occur in every basis, and compact-element bases are smallest.

items.title: Continuous, algebraic, omega-continuous, and omega-algebraic domains
items.summary: The exact domain predicates combine partial-order dcpo structure with the corresponding basis condition; preorder-level basis components remain separately reusable.

items.title: Characterizing continuous and algebraic domains
items.summary: Continuity is equivalent to the whole carrier being a basis; algebraicity is compact-element basis formation.

items.title: Inductive closure systems
items.summary: A closure system is inductive when it is closed under directed unions.

items.title: Inductive closure systems are algebraic
items.summary: Finitely generated hulls supply compact approximants for inductive closure systems.

items.title: Order through basis approximants
items.summary: For a basis, `x ≤ y` can be tested by inclusion of the approximants below `x` into those below `y`.

items.title: Basis criterion for Scott-continuity
items.summary: Scott-continuity can be checked using basis elements and finite approximation witnesses.

items.title: Omega-basis fixed point chains
items.summary: A countable basis supports an omega-chain description of continuous least fixed points; the full cited theorem is recorded as an external axiom.

items.title: Countable bases and omega-chains
items.summary: Countable bases reduce directed supremum arguments to cofinal omega-chains.

items.title: Omega-ccpos and omega-continuity
items.summary: Continuous or algebraic omega-ccpos are dcpos, and omega-continuous maps are continuous under the stated hypotheses.

items.title: Interpolation
items.summary: Way-below interpolation, including finite and basis-refined forms.

items.title: Way-below and directed suprema
items.summary: Way-below elements of a directed supremum are already below a member of the directed set.

items.title: Principal ideals and locality
items.summary: Continuity, algebraicity, compactness, and way-below tests can be localized to principal ideals.

items.title: Compact elements and finite joins
items.summary: Minimal upper bounds and finite joins preserve compactness under the chapter's local hypotheses.

items.title: Algebraic complete lattices
items.summary: A complete lattice is algebraic exactly when every element is a join of compact elements below it.

items.title: Abstract bases
items.summary: Abstract bases are transitive approximation structures with finite interpolation.

items.title: Ideals and ideal completion
items.summary: Lower directed ideals over an abstract basis, the ideal completion, and principal ideals.

items.title: Properties of ideal completion
items.summary: Ideal completions are dcpos; their way-below relation, basis, continuity, algebraicity, and compact basis behavior are formalized.

items.title: Products of abstract bases
items.summary: Ideal completion preserves products for the local abstract-basis construction.

items.title: Extension from ideal completions
items.summary: Constructs the largest Scott-continuous extension, exposes its directed-supremum formula and reflexive-basis equality, and proves that the assignment f ↦ fhat is Scott-continuous.

items.title: Continuous domains as ideal completions
items.summary: A partial-order dcpo with a concrete basis is represented by the ideal completion of its extracted abstract basis.

items.title: Maps determined by basis values
items.summary: Continuous maps from a continuous domain are determined by their values on a basis.

items.title: Approximable relations
items.summary: Approximable relations between abstract bases, used for categorical representation statements.

items.title: Abstract bases and continuous domains
items.summary: The PDF-level result is stated as a mathlib bundled equivalence between the category of abstract bases and approximable relations and the category of continuous dcpos and Scott-continuous maps.

items.title: Preorders and algebraic domains
items.summary: The PDF-level result is stated as a mathlib bundled equivalence between reflexive abstract bases and algebraic dcpos with Scott-continuous maps.

items.title: Scott topology
items.summary: Scott-closed and Scott-open sets, the source-facing unbundled topology, a mathlib TopologicalSpace bridge, interiors, and neighborhoods.

items.title: Order and separation from Scott topology
items.summary: The Scott topology reconstructs the specialization order; T0 and Hausdorff separation are characterized locally.

items.title: Directed suprema by Scott neighborhoods
items.summary: A directed supremum is characterized by upper-bound status plus meeting every Scott neighborhood.

items.title: Order-theoretic and topological Scott-continuity
items.summary: The two formulations of Scott-continuity coincide for the unbundled Scott topologies.

items.title: Way-below and Scott interiors
items.summary: In continuous domains, approximation is equivalent to membership in the Scott interior, and to membership in `↑↑x`.

items.title: Scott opens from way-below support
items.summary: Scott-open sets are supported by way-below elements, and by basis elements in the basis-refined form.

items.title: Scott opens of ideal completions
items.summary: Scott-open subsets of an ideal completion arise from observable opens determined by basis subsets.

items.title: Scott opens as unions of filters
items.summary: Scott-open sets in continuous domains are unions of Scott-open filters, using an interpolating sequence.
